name: Drunkenness and Gluttony

counsel.text: A gracious person holds the golden bridle of temperance; he takes his meat as a medicine to heal the decays of nature, that he may be the fitter, by the strength he receives, for the service of God; he makes his food, not fuel for lust, but help to duty.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, man's chief end

counsel.text: Consider what ways, what companies, what opportunities, what studies, what businesses, what conditions, have at any time given, or do usually give, advantages to thy distempers, and set thyself heedfully against them all. Men will do this with respect unto their bodily infirmities and distempers. The seasons, the diet, the air that have proved offensive shall be avoided. Are the things of the soul of less importance?
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: God allows recruits of nature, and what may fit us the better for his service; but beware of surfeit. Excess in the creature clouds the mind, chokes good affections, and provokes lust.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: It is easier to obey the commands of God than sin. The commands of sin are burdensome -- let a man be under the power of any lust, how he tires himself! what hazards he runs, even to endangering his health and soul, that he may satisfy his lusts!
counsel.author: Thomas Watson

counsel.text: He died to destroy the works of the devil. Whatever came upon our natures by his first temptation, whatever receives strength in our persons by his daily suggestions, Christ died to destroy it all.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Father, I have sinned against you. I let my appetite rule me, and I went to food and drink for what only you can give. I do not hide it or excuse it. You have promised to forgive and cleanse all who confess their sins to you, and so I come. I rest on the blood of Jesus Christ, who is my Advocate with you and the atoning sacrifice for my sins. Wash me again. Holy Spirit, make me hate this sin itself, not only what it costs me. Teach me to eat and drink to your glory, with thanks, and to find my rest and gladness in Christ. Amen.

prayers.title: When the craving is strong
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, the craving is strong right now, and I am weak. You are the bread of life, and you satisfy as nothing on this table or in this cup ever can. I come to you now. Do not let this appetite be my master, for I belong to you, body and soul. Holy Spirit, fill me instead, and give me self-control, which is your fruit and not my own. Give me strength to put this down and walk away right now. Amen.

prayers.title: For freedom from bondage
prayers.text: Father, you gave food and drink as good gifts, and I have let them become my masters. I do not want to be ruled by my belly or my cup. Break this bondage now by the power of Christ's cross. Holy Spirit, give me a sober mind and a clear heart, so that I can pray and do my duty. Keep me from the places, the company, and the hours that lead me into excess, and turn my hunger toward you. Amen.

examinationQuestions: When you reached for more today, what were you really hungry or thirsty for: comfort, escape, relief from worry, or company?
Have you been treating food or drink as a refuge, a place to run to that belongs to God alone?
What places, people, hours, or moods have most often led you into excess, and have you set yourself against them?
Are you receiving food and drink with thanks, and using them so that you are more fit to serve God, not less?
Is there anyone you have hidden this from who should know, such as your pastor or a brother or sister in your church?
If you find you cannot stop, or your body seems to depend on drink, have you told your pastor and seen a doctor?
fleeActions: Put the drink or the food away, close the cupboard, and leave the room.
Leave the place or the company that is drawing you toward excess. Give a plain reason and go home.
Drink a glass of water, then step outside and walk for ten minutes, praying as you go.
Call or text a brother or sister in your church and tell them plainly that you are tempted right now.
Open your Bible to John 6 and read it slowly, out loud if you can.
If you have tried to stop and cannot, call your pastor today, and make an appointment with a doctor if your body may depend on drink.

afterFallReadings.text: Consider his mercifulness, tenderness, and kindness, as he is our great High Priest at the right hand of God. Assuredly he pities thee in thy distress; saith he, "As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you," Isa. 66:13. He hath the tenderness of a mother to a sucking child.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

afterFallReadings.text: The people of God have sins of daily occurrence; and, besides these, they sometimes lapse into great sins, and God is provoked, and his justice is ready to break forth upon them: but Christ's intercession is ready at hand, he daily makes up the breaches between God and them; he presents the merits of his blood to his Father, to pacify him.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office
